title: What is known about 1RB1RE_0LC1RF_---1LD_1LE0LD_1LA1LB_1RF0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_0LC1RF_---1LD_1LE0LD_1LA1LB_1RF0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head sweeps the whole tape. To the right the tape is long domains of 10 separated by short defects 111 0101 or 111 (01)^4; to the left a repeating structure of period about 20 and a comb of period 10. The rightward sweeps over 10 and 1011 are proved shift rules; the evolution of the domains is not known. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide, and proves the shift rules of the sweeps (lean/Rules.lean); the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,589 cells have been visited and 26,006 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.347). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: The rightward sweeps: L A> (1011)^n R (each 1011 becomes 1010), L A> (10)^n R (pairs left as they are) and L 1 E> (01)^n R (each 01 becomes 10), for every n and all tapes L, R.

claims.title: Domains of 10 on the right
claims.text: At step 1,036,291,430 (width 37,589, right end) the tape ends in domains (10)^142, (10)^2512, (10)^12108, (10)^282, (10)^286 separated by 111 (01)^4 or 111 0101, after a comb (1010101110)^656 and a left part repeating 111 (01)^4 (10)^6. Seen at the end turns; not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts on C0, reached as 0 B>0 (B reads 0 with a 0 to its left, and moves onto it). Inside a domain of 10 the sweeps never do that; whether a defect ever does is open.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RA_1RC1RD_1LD1LB_0RF1LE_1LE0LC_---1RA up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The right side of the tape is long runs of the pair 10, broken by short defects; the left side repeats a pattern about twenty cells long. The head crosses the runs by proved rules, but how the runs change has not been worked out.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 37,589 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
The longest domain of 10 at step 10<sup>9</sup>.

sections.heading: A periodic left part, domains on the right
html: Two end turns, long runs written as powers:

The left part repeats a word of about 20 cells (111 (01)^4 (10)^6 after a rightward sweep), then comes a comb of period 10 and then the domains of 10. The rightward sweeps over 10 and 1011 are proved shift rules (lean/Rules.lean).

sections.heading: Domains that grow and split
html: The domains of 10 grow fast (4840 pairs at step 2.2·108, 12,108 at step 109) and new defects appear between them; at step 1,036,291,430 they are 142, 2512, 12108, 282, 286 pairs. No rule for their evolution has been found.

sections.heading: One pattern at a defect
html: C0 is the only halting transition, reached as 0 B>0. It never happens inside a domain; whether a defect ever produces it is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.347). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,589 cells (2,043 left of the start, 26,644 right), with a density of 1s of 0.692.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A bouncer whose right part is long runs of the pairs 10 separated by the defect 111 0101, and whose left part is a period-20 structure followed by a period-10 comb; the runs on the right grow and split unevenly, with no known rule.
family: bouncer with 10 domains, periodic left part
